reader.notes: The screen refuses a pseudo-text-1 whose match words (every element but separator commas/semicolons and directive lines) number zero, which is SR3 and SR7 together. The diagnostic text cites §2023:7.2.4.3 SR3 at --std 85 rather than §1985:XII.3.3 SR3 (the requirement is the same; message quality only). The scanner's DirectiveLine kind is edition-blind, so a >>-line inside pseudo-text at 85 would count as space; not probed, outside this rule's ordinary range.

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-073/q1gtgt.cob (--std 85, fixed): REPLACE == / a line '           >>XYZ' / == BY ==MOVE "HIT" TO W==. printed EXIT 65: 'q1gtgt.cob(8,20): error COBOL2572: REPLACE statement: pseudo-text-1 holds no text-word to match - §2023:7.2.4.3 SR3' plus COBOL2572 (§2023:7.2.4.3 SR10 directive line inside operand) and COBOL2697 (§2023:7.3.3 SR8 b). q2gtgt.cob (same with >>PAGE) adds COBOL0900 and the same SR3 refusal. Control q4gtx.cob: ==>>XYZ== on the REPLACE line compiles and runs '[OK  ]' (the text word is counted when it does not start a line). At 1985 there are no compiler directive lines: '>>XYZ' is a text word, '(3) Any other sequence of contiguous COBOL characters except comment lines and the word 'COPY', bounded by separators' (OK §1985:III.2, the text is in the clause), and '>' is a COBOL character ('| > | greater than symbol |', OK §1985:III.2). So pseudo-text-1 holds one text word and 'Pseudo-text-1 must contain one or more text words' (OK §1985:XII.3.3 SR3) is satisfied; the compiler refuses it with the SR3 diagnostic itself. Cause: TextWordScanner.TryNext classifies a line-initial '>>word' as TextWordKind.DirectiveLine through CompilerDirectiveLine.TryParse with no edition test, and Operand.MatchWords drops DirectiveLine (TextWord.IsSpaceForMatching), so the SR3 count is 0 at 85. At --std 2023 the same program draws the same three errors, which is right there (a directive line, SR10). kb/Work search (DirectiveLine, COBOL2697, '>>' with 1985): PB1353, PB1352, PB1384 cover the 2023 directive-in-pseudo-text rules; no note names the 1985 text-word case. The reader saw the risk ('a >>-line inside pseudo-text at 85 would count as space; not probed').
